items.title: Les problèmes privés qui ont gâché le début de saison de Thorgan Hazard
items.summary: Thorgan Hazard a enfin pu faire la différence au RC Lens. L'ancien joueur d'Anderlecht a été décisif ce samedi face au Paris FC avec un assist et un but, permettant à son équipe de renverser la vapeur pour s'imposer 2-1. Après des mois durant lesquels peu de choses semblaient tourner rond, cette solide prestation est arrivée à point nommé pour le Belge de 33 ans.

items.title: Somers neemt het na eerste zege sinds augustus op voor trainer Compper: "Zijn hand wordt steeds duidelijker"
items.summary: De eerste overwinning sinds augustus heeft Antwerp opnieuw wat ademruimte gegeven, maar de Great Old is er nog lang niet. Na vijf opeenvolgende nederlagen blijft bevestiging noodzakelijk. Thibo Somers ziet intussen steeds meer de hand van trainer Marvin Compper in het spel en neemt het op voor zijn coach.

items.title: Battre Anderlecht 4-0, ça soulage : "Tout le monde a dit qu'on avait eu de la chance, mais..."
items.summary: La Gantoise a facilement pris la mesure du Sporting d'Anderlecht ce dimanche à la Planet Group Arena : 4-0. Les Buffalos demeurent en tête de la Jupiler Pro League après neuf journées. Rik De Mil est donc un entraîneur satisfait après une semaine difficile, mais il ne veut toutefois pas s'emballer et garde les pieds sur terre.

items.title: Club Brugge staat nu echt tussen de grootheden en verbreekt eigen record
items.summary: Club Brugge heeft een belangrijke stap gezet in de UEFA-clubranking. Blauw-zwart is daarin voorbij twee Portugese grootmachten, FC Porto en Sporting CP, gegaan. Ook Tottenham sneuvelde en zo doet Club Brugge het ongezien goed. Nooit stonden ze hoger op de UEFA-ranglijsten.

items.title: Genk jubile : "Je sais ce que ça fait aux supporters de battre le Standard"
items.summary: En supériorité numérique pendant plus d'une heure, le Racing Genk s'est imposé face au Standard, ce dimanche (2-1). Tout n'était pas parfait, mais l'entraîneur limbourgeois Jess Thorup se montrait néanmoins satisfait après ce troisième succès de rang.

items.title: Vitor Bruno en Vincent Euvrard onder druk: code rood bij Anderlecht en Standard
items.summary: Anderlecht en Standard gingen afgelopen weekend onderuit. Daardoor staan Vitor Bruno en Vincent Euvrard voor twee wedstrijden die bijzonder zwaar kunnen doorwegen. Punten pakken is noodzakelijk, niet alleen voor het klassement, maar ook om het vertrouwen van bestuur en achterban te behouden richting de volgende interlandbreak.

items.title: Eén speler viel door de mand, Leko zet zijn spelers op scherp met strenge boodschap: "Stay humble, work hard"
items.summary: Club Brugge wil dit seizoen geen steken laten vallen. Zonder play-offs telt elk puntenverlies dubbel in de titelstrijd en dat beseft ook Ivan Leko maar al te goed. De trainer zag zijn ploeg tegen STVV een moeilijke eerste helft afwerken, maar was tevreden over de reactie na rust. Zijn boodschap is duidelijk: gas terugnemen is geen optie en niemand is zeker van zijn plaats.

items.title: Surprise à Newcastle : pourquoi Matias Fernandez-Pardo était-il absent de la feuille de match ?

items.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
items.summary: Bournemouth’s transfer nous puts United to shame, Araújo is winning admirers at Anfield and Suzuki adapts swiftly at Villa The three Bournemouth goalscorers cost a combined £85m, joining from Vasco da Gama, Middlesbrough, and Porto. The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. items.title: Terland strikes late as United end Manchester City’s winning start in WSL
items.summary: At long last, a weakness has been spotted. Finally, the 100% winning start ends for Manchester City, much to the pleasure of Manchester United, who struck late through Elisabeth Terland to claim a point in a well-contested and at times breathless derby. Khadija “Bunny” Shaw’s second-half strike – her 91st WSL goal on her 100th appearance in the division – appeared to have settled the game and kept the defending champions top of the table, and it had looked likely to be the same old story, of City finding a way to win a game that was on a knife-edge, because they have the game’s deadliest finisher. items.title: Pierre Sage regrets ‘missed 15 minutes’ as defeat increases heat on Crystal Palace manager
items.summary: Sage’s side beaten 2-0 at home by Newcastle ‘Every mistake that is bad will be a goal’ Pierre Sage blamed a 15-minute loss of concentration for Crystal Palace’s 2-0 defeat by Newcastle and insisted he remains the right man to lead the south London club. “We missed 15 minutes when we came back from the dressing room,” the Frenchman said. “When you let your opponent take the initiative without pressure, without reply, it’s difficult.” Palace have conceded 19 goals in eight games and have the worst defensive record in the Premier League, an obvious contrast to last season when Sage’s Lens side had the second-best defensive record in Ligue 1. “When we concede all these goals … you can interpret that through the style of play and also how well we are playing, especially defensively,” Sage said. items.title: Fernandes gamble leaves Carrick to carry the can for United’s institutional failures | Will Unwin
items.summary: Leaving out his captain was doomed to fail but so are the club under the current leadership and the fans at Old Trafford know that all too well Dropping your captain, who has held the team together for most of the past five years, is a bold move from a man whose job is on the line. It was very much a make-or-break decision from Michael Carrick to leave out Bruno Fernandes against Bournemouth. It did not work and Carrick knew the consequences if it failed and will probably pay the price for it, but he should not be alone. Carrick said the decision to drop the Portuguese playmaker was purely based on football reasons but criticising his manager after the desperate defeat to Como cannot have helped. Clearly Carrick disagreed with his captain’s comments on the lack of pressing in the Champions League fixture. It was somewhat telling that Lisandro Martínez kept his place despite pointing out the director of football, Jason Wilcox, was a hindrance to the club the previous week. Continue reading...

items.title: Isak applies finishing touch as Liverpool bring Brighton’s winning run to an end
items.summary: Brighton’s impressive run was blown off course at Anfield where Liverpool performed with an appetite and urgency at both ends of the pitch that showed Andoni Iraola’s methods taking root. It was Liverpool, deserving winners on home soil for the first time in the Premier League this season, who looked upwardly mobile. There was more evidence of the expensive trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola feeling at home and adapting to Iraola’s demands. Wirtz was instrumental in an opening goal officially credited to Brighton’s Pascal Gross and Isak scored for the sixth time in six Premier League appearances to shatter the visitors’ sequence of four successive league wins. The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break.
